title: Markdown rendering with sanitization

requirements.text: Markdown (CommonMark plus the tables/task lists the app supports) renders to HTML
Rendered HTML, including any raw HTML in the source, is sanitized with an allowlist on the trusted side before storage or display
Link and image URLs are limited to safe schemes (no javascript:, data:, vbscript:), including mixed-case and entity-encoded variants
User links get rel="noopener noreferrer nofollow" (or equivalent) to prevent tabnabbing and link spam
Code blocks and inline code are escaped, and syntax highlighting cannot reintroduce markup
Input size and nesting are bounded so pathological Markdown cannot exhaust CPU or memory

implementations.notes: Allowlist sanitizers (DOMPurify, nh3, bluemonday ...) with a 15-payload XSS corpus in per-language suites under examples/cookbook; no tests/ test runs them. It sanitizes HTML, so it applies to the renderer output
External CommonMark parser; pair it with the sanitizer

notes: Genlib has no Markdown-to-HTML renderer. recipe:markdown-to-plaintext-excerpt strips Markdown to text and recipe:html-escape-and-safe-template has a tested URL allow-list, but neither renders Markdown.
